history.summary: The Anantheshwara Temple on Car Street (Ratha Beedi), immediately beside the Sri Krishna Matha, is among the oldest temples in the Tulu Nadu region, built during the reign of the Alupa dynasty in the 8th century CE. In an inscription dated 1357 CE the deity is referred to as the 'Mahadeva of Udupi'. Legend credits the sage Parashurama with establishing the temple, and a local account says King Ramabhoja installed the linga on a silver pedestal (Rajata Pitha) after accidentally killing a snake, to atone for sarpa dosha — the name Anantheshwara links Ananta (the serpent) to Shiva. It is the temple where Madhvacharya is said to have worshipped and taught his disciples before founding the Krishna Matha, and devotees customarily visit it before the Krishna temple. The sanctum is in the gajaprashta (elephant-back) form; a unique feature is the Nandi statue facing away from the sanctum. Its architecture is classic coastal/Kerala style with granite and wooden carving.

town_description: Udupi is a coastal city in Tulu Nadu, Karnataka, best known as the birthplace of the Dvaita school of Vedanta and home to the famous Sri Krishna Matha. It is a major pilgrimage city whose temple streets draw lakhs of devotees, and it is also famous nationwide for Udupi vegetarian cuisine. Malpe beach lies about 6 km away, and the city is well connected by rail and road to Mangaluru and Bengaluru.
